# APA Results Reporting {background-color="#275882"}

## Why APA Format Matters

::: {.definition-box}
**APA Style**: The official style guide of the American Psychological Association, providing standards for scientific writing and reporting.
:::

## Reporting Statistical Tests

::: {.example-box}
**t-test example**:

> There was a significant difference in scores between the caffeine group (*M* = 85.2, *SD* = 12.4) and the control group (*M* = 72.8, *SD* = 14.1), *t*(58) = 3.45, *p* = .001, *d* = 0.89.
:::

## Key Elements to Include

::: {.incremental}
- Descriptive statistics (M, SD)
- Test statistic and degrees of freedom
- p-value (exact or inequality)
- Effect size
- Confidence intervals where appropriate
:::

## Common Reporting Formats

::: {.panel-tabset}

### t-test

*t*(df) = X.XX, *p* = .XXX, *d* = X.XX

### Correlation

*r*(df) = .XX, *p* = .XXX

### ANOVA

*F*(df1, df2) = X.XX, *p* = .XXX, partial eta-squared = .XX

:::

## Formatting Tips

::: {.callout-tip}
## Remember
- Italicise statistical symbols (*M*, *SD*, *t*, *p*, *r*, *F*)
- Use leading zero for statistics that can exceed 1 (e.g., *M* = 0.75)
- No leading zero for statistics bounded by 1 (e.g., *p* = .023, *r* = .45)
:::
